newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products were steady, but trade slow.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products were steady, but trade slow.

text.p: Med oil products were subdued but steady on Friday.
Gasoline markets were relatively quiet. A 98/88 unleaded cargo was heard traded on Thursday at $19 over premium unleaded barge quotes, cif southern France.
High octane interest remains into Lavera, where MTBE production has been cut back.

Naphtha prices were resilient as traders bid on the swaps market. Petrochemical demand is still good and alternative feedstocks -- propane traded in the Med at $259 cif Italy -- remain far too expensive to serve as an alternative to naphtha.
Gas oil was fairly subdued. Traders said buyers were holding out to see whether prices will ease with the arrival of north American gas oil in Europe over the next two weeks.
Despite the quiet market, traders said there was plenty of potential demand out of Greek, Turkey, Spain and Italy.

The Greek winter tender closes on Tuesday and some traders think the country will take far more than the 500,000-600,000 tonnes stated in the original buy tender. Traders said bids would be in the quotes cif high to cif high +$1.50 range.
Russian material remained thin. Traders put premiums at quotes cif high +$2.50/+$3.50, basis Genoa.
